items.stem: How many points should a story try to make?

options.label: One clear point
As many as possible
Five or more

items.hint_text: A story that says everything says nothing.
items.feedback_correct: Yes. One clear point keeps the reader focused on what matters.
items.feedback_wrong: A story that tries to say many things says nothing. Committing to one point keeps the reader focused on what matters.

items.stem: Which opening commits to a single point?

options.label: Bus waits are longest exactly when students need them most.
Buses, schedules, and neighborhoods are all interesting.
Here is everything we collected this month.

items.hint_text: A point is a claim you can check.
items.feedback_correct: Right. The first opening makes one claim you can check.
items.feedback_wrong: Only the first option makes one claim you could check. The others list topics instead of stating a point.

items.stem: Which sentences state a single point a story could make? Select all that apply.

options.label: The library closes before most students finish studying.
We gathered many facts about the library.
The crossing is unsafe during the morning rush.
There are several topics about the neighborhood.

items.hint_text: A point is a claim, not an announcement of topics.
items.feedback_correct: Yes. The closing time and the unsafe crossing are both checkable claims.
items.feedback_wrong: A point is a claim you can check, like the closing time or the unsafe crossing. The other options only announce that topics exist.

items.stem: What does the module call a claim without evidence?

options.label: An opinion wearing a headline
A strong finding
A finished story

items.hint_text: Think about how a bare claim is described.
items.feedback_correct: Correct. Without evidence a claim is only an opinion wearing a headline.
items.feedback_wrong: Without evidence a claim is only an opinion dressed up as a headline. It is not a finding or a finished story until real data supports it.

items.stem: Which items count as evidence for a claim about bus waits? Select all that apply.

options.label: Times you recorded at the bus stop
A count of students waiting each morning
Your feeling that buses are slow
A friend saying buses seem late

items.hint_text: Evidence is data you actually collected.
items.feedback_correct: Right. Recorded times and counts are data you actually collected.
items.feedback_wrong: Evidence is data you actually collected, like recorded times or counts. Feelings and hearsay are opinions, not evidence for the claim.

items.stem: What should you do with material that does not support your one point?

options.label: Cut it from the story
Keep it to add length
Add a second point to use it

items.hint_text: Anything that does not support the point weakens the story.
items.feedback_correct: Yes. Cutting unsupported material keeps the reader on the single message.
items.feedback_wrong: Extra material that does not support the point weakens the story. Cutting it keeps the reader on the single message.

items.stem: Which opening makes one clear claim?

options.label: Students miss class most often on the coldest mornings.
Weather, buses, and classes are all worth studying.
We looked at a lot of information this week.

items.hint_text: Look for the specific, checkable claim.
items.feedback_correct: Correct. The first option states one checkable claim about absences and cold mornings.
items.feedback_wrong: The first option states one checkable claim about absences and cold mornings. The others list topics without making a point.

items.stem: Which openings commit to a single point? Select all that apply.

options.label: The corner store raised prices twice this year.
The park is busiest right after school.
Parks, stores, and prices are interesting.
We collected many notes.

items.hint_text: A single point is a specific claim you can check.
items.feedback_correct: Right. The price change and the busy hours are both specific claims.
items.feedback_wrong: A single point is a specific claim you can check, like prices or busy hours. The last two options only say that topics exist.

items.stem: Your story claims the park is busy after school. What backs it best?

options.label: Counts of people in the park each afternoon
A colorful photo of one person
Your belief that it seems busy

items.hint_text: Match the evidence to the claim.
items.feedback_correct: Yes. Counts taken at that time show the pattern the claim describes.
items.feedback_wrong: A claim about how busy the park is needs counts taken at that time. A single photo or a belief does not show the pattern the claim describes.

items.stem: Why does a story need evidence behind its point?

options.label: Otherwise the point is just an opinion
To make the story longer
To avoid choosing a point

items.hint_text: Evidence is what turns a claim into a finding.
items.feedback_correct: Correct. Evidence is what turns a claim into a finding.
items.feedback_wrong: Evidence is what turns a claim into a finding. Length and avoiding a point are not reasons to gather evidence.
